upheld.detail: The new <a> around the order number is not covered by any style: Orders.razor.css has no rule for .order-number a and app.css has no general link style. upheld.detail: Video 06 shows 'Order not found' with the caption 'Order not found (HTTP 404)', but no frame or caption names the order number that was requested, so you can't tell from the video that it is the 999999 case.

upheld.title: Coverage gap
upheld.detail: The style coverage table marks '.editorconfig via dotnet format --verify-no-changes' as unverifiable: the command was not run, and the judge could not run it either. No finding covered it. Nothing in the diff looks misformatted.

dismissed.title: Order summary has no heading
dismissed.reason: Withdrawn by the critic. The story's Outputs require only that the number, date, status and total are shown, and they are (OrderDetails.razor:19-42). A summary heading is a preference.

dismissed.title: Back-link arrow icon has no alt attribute
dismissed.reason: Withdrawn by the critic. role="presentation" already removes the decorative arrow from the accessibility tree, and the back link has its text label 'Back to my orders'.

upheld.detail: The demo.highlight caption under the order-number link is cut off at the left edge of the viewport and reads 'r 1 links to /user/orders/1', so its first words are missing. The page that follows is the correct details page; only the narration is affected.
upheld.requirement: AC1: When he opens My orders and follows the link of that order number Then the details page shows ...

upheld.title: A test passes only on a retry in CI: [scenarios] › e2e/teststack/ordd-1.spec.ts:159:5 › TC-ORDD-1-06 order number that does not exist shows Order not found with 404
A test passes only on a retry in CI: [scenarios] › e2e/teststack/ordd-1.spec.ts:218:5 › TC-ORDD-1-10 order number 0 shows Order not found with 404
Order number above int range does not show 'Order not found'
upheld.detail: The page route uses {orderNumber:int}. A positive whole order number above 2147483647 (e.g. /user/orders/9999999999) matches no route, so the WebApp sends a bare 404 with no layout and no 'Order not found' text instead of the page the story describes for an order number that does not exist.
upheld.requirement: For an order number that does not exist ... the page shows exactly `Order not found` and responds with HTTP status 404.

upheld.title: Order-number link on My orders has no visible link cue at rest
upheld.detail: The new order-number anchor uses the body ink color and weight with no underline, and the underline appears only on hover. A shopper, especially on a touch device, cannot tell that the number opens the order's details page. Other in-content text links in the app (.in-cart a) are underlined at rest.
upheld.requirement: ORDD-1 Outputs: 'On the My orders page, each order number is a link to that order's details page'

upheld.title: TC-01 link caption clipped off the left edge
upheld.detail: The green caption under the highlighted order number starts outside the viewport and reads '· links to /user/orders/1', so its beginning is cut off; the same defect was fixed for TC-08 but remains here.
upheld.requirement: On the My orders page, each order number is a link to that order's details page, /user/orders/{orderNumber}.

upheld.title: TC-07 frames can't tell the foreign-order case from a missing order
upheld.detail: Frame 07/frame-002.png@2.3 shows the AC4 result: 'Order not found', no order data, caption 'alice's order 2 (HTTP 404)'. No frame shows who is signed in, only a generic user icon, so the recording looks the same as TC-06's missing-order case. Only the caption says the order belongs to someone else.
upheld.requirement: Given alice has placed an order When bob opens the details page of alice's order number Then the page shows Order not found with status 404

dismissed.title: Shared order-row styles moved from scoped CSS to global app.css
dismissed.reason: Withdrawn by the critic. Sharing the order-row rules via app.css was an earlier PR-check fix to remove duplication, and I found no convention violation that warrants reinstating it.

dismissed.title: Attribute type declared inside an extensions file
dismissed.reason: Withdrawn by the critic. Placing a small marker attribute next to the middleware that consumes it is a placement preference, not a broken guideline.

upheld.evidence: src/WebApp/Components/Pages/User/OrderDetails.razor:1; PR description Follow-ups ('unknown URLs return a bare 404 with no layout')

upheld.title: Product column wraps while numeric columns have spare width
upheld.detail: The items list reuses `.orders-item > div { flex: 1 0 0 }`, so all four columns are equal width. Product names, the longest content, wrap onto two lines ('Wanderer Black Hiking / Boots') while Unit price, Units and Line total leave wide empty gaps, which makes the item rows look uneven.
upheld.requirement: ORDD-1 Outputs: 'one row per item with the product name, the unit price, the number of units and the line total'; layout should match neighbouring components

dismissed.reason: The story only requires the order number to be a link to /user/orders/{n}, and it is (Orders.razor:42, e2e TC-01). dismissed.reason: Withdrawn by the critic. A small attribute that exists only to mark endpoints for the middleware in the same file is a reasonable grouping, and no repository rule requires one type per file.
